messages:
sam: Quick follow-up on the coalescer batch policy RFC — does everyone agree we should switch to lease-based rebalance for short streams to avoid head-of-line blocking? thinking... :thinking:

maria: +1 for lease rebalance for < 2s streams, but worried about extra RPCs and churn on control plane

lee: Can you outline the failure modes? If we rebalance leases aggressively we might cause repeated KV-cache invalidations and token checkpoints

sam: good point. failure modes I care about: 1) repeated reassigns causing duplicate mid-flight tokens, 2) scheduler churn making steady-state latency worse. Proposal: only rebalance when inflight < 50 and stream idle > 200ms

pat: nit: 50 seems arbitrary. What's the cost model? If rebalance prevents head-of-line, but costs 10ms RPC, net savings only if waiting would've cost >10ms

maria: cost model: RPC ~5–8ms p50 within region, KV invalidation cost depends on model length. We measured ~20ms tail for small streams when head-of-line happens

lee: alternative: coalesce multiple short streams into one lease for same tenant for 100ms window. reduces reassigns but loses per-call isolation

nik: +1 to coalescer idea but we need auth isolation. Could we attach light-weight context header that carries per-request auth but share lease? ensures audit

sam: sounds promising. Can we prototype: (a) lease rebalance with hysteresis; (b) coalesce-mode gated by tenant flag. I'll open a PR for 2 small patches

sam: proposal config snippet:
```
coalesce_window_ms=100
rebalance_idle_ms=200
inflight_threshold=50
```

opsbot: deploy-bot: branch 'edge/coalesce-proto' CI started — will report back

pat: also add metric for 'rebalance_count' and 'kv_invalidate_latency' so we can A/B

maria: agree, let's A/B for 2 weeks. If p95 latency improves by >5% we keep

lee: one more: ensure that fallback to non-coalesce path preserves idempotency headers. otherwise side-effects risk

sam: yep. will add checklist in PR. thx everyone :thumbsup:
